simulated: All PM state, agent replies, document revisions, connection changes and speech recognition are SIMULATED by the mockup. Inputs are real simulator touchpad actions.

journeys.title: Read a spec, discuss it in its session, revise, approve, hand back to PM

shots.title: Needs you
shots.caption: Root view lists what is waiting for the user: a spec and a plan to review, a QA scenario that needs input, a manual merge.

shots.title: Spec under review
shots.caption: Long-form reading in native text. The footer keeps document identity, version and review state on every page.

shots.title: Reading the ambiguities
shots.caption: Pages break at bullets and headings. Page 4 of 5 starts at the section the reviewer wants to discuss.

shots.title: Speaking to the spec’s own session
shots.caption: Hold to speak. The panel names the target session (#214 impl) and the page; the document above stays in place.

shots.title: Review before sending
shots.caption: Recognized text is reviewed before it is sent. The message carries the document version, hash, section and page.

shots.title: Sent; reading continues
shots.caption: Sending returns to the same page. Nothing is resent automatically.

shots.title: Document actions
shots.caption: Discuss opens the existing impl session. Approval is offered only for the version on screen.

shots.title: Discussion in the existing session
shots.caption: The impl session that wrote the spec, not a new chat. The user’s message shows the context it was sent with; the reply streams.

shots.title: Revision delivered
shots.caption: The session rewrote the spec. PM sees a new content hash (v3 · 9a07).

shots.title: Back on the same page; v2 is no longer current
shots.caption: Back returns to page 4 of v2. A banner says v3 exists. The reader does not jump to v3 on its own.

shots.title: Approval needs the current version
shots.caption: v2 cannot be approved once it has been replaced. "What changed" is offered instead.

shots.title: What changed v2 → v3
shots.caption: Changed and added items, by requirement or ambiguity id. Each one opens v3 at that item.

shots.title: Re-review v3 at the change
shots.caption: v3 opens at A1. The footer shows v3 is the version under review.

shots.title: Approve the version read
shots.caption: The approve row names the version and its content hash.

shots.title: Explicit confirmation
shots.caption: Confirmation states what approval does: implementation resumes unattended, the automated phases follow, and merge stays manual.

shots.title: Handed back to PM
shots.caption: Approval releases the spec hold. PM runs implementation, review, QA and sign-off with no agent windows to drive. Only the merge hold remains.

shots.title: Progress without intervention
shots.caption: 47 minutes later (simulated): implementation and two review iterations finished, and QA is running. The user did nothing in between.

journeys.title: Every PM session: open a QA scenario and its verifier, discuss, return without duplicates

shots.title: PR status
shots.caption: PR #215 in QA. Its QA spec and every session are one step away.

shots.title: Reading the QA spec
shots.caption: An approved QA spec. Scenario s2 says the banner clears "within two polls".

shots.title: #215 sessions
shots.caption: Implementation, review, the QA run and sign-off, each with its own state. QA is one entry per run that opens its sessions.

shots.title: QA run 2
shots.caption: Planner, the interactive session s0, each scenario with its own state (verifying, needs input, retrying, queued), and finalize.

shots.title: Scenario s2 sessions
shots.caption: The refiner, execution worker and verifier are separate sessions in window qa-#215-s2. The verifier is working.

shots.title: Verifier session, opened not launched
shots.caption: Opening an existing session attaches to it. Nothing new starts. The header gives PR, run, scenario, role and live state.

shots.title: Asking the busy verifier
shots.caption: The verifier is busy, so the message joins its queue in the same session.

shots.title: Queued, not duplicated
shots.caption: The follow-up is queued in the verifier’s own session. No second verifier.

shots.title: Inspecting the ongoing verification
shots.caption: The reply arrives in place. The verifier flags the timing, and PM’s existing retry sends the worker back.

shots.title: Session actions
shots.caption: From any session: speak, the scenario’s other sessions, all PR sessions, or straight back to the document it came from.

shots.title: Switch to the s2 worker
shots.caption: Switching moves within scenario s2. The worker shows the re-capture the verifier asked for.

shots.title: A relaunched scenario
shots.caption: s4’s worker was relaunched (retry 1). Its refiner pane is gone, and its verifier appears only after the first PASS.

shots.title: A scenario that needs input
shots.caption: s3’s refiner rejected the scenario. It needs a decision, so it is also listed in Needs you.

shots.title: Refiner s3
shots.caption: The refiner explains what it needs. The user could answer by voice here.

shots.title: Back to the originating document
shots.caption: One action returns to the QA spec at the same page, through any number of session switches.

shots.title: Starting a session is explicit
shots.caption: Sign-off is not running. Starting it names its side effect (qa → sign_off). Opening never starts anything.

shots.title: Starting…
shots.caption: One request is in flight. The row shows ◐ starting.

shots.title: Repeated taps join the request
shots.caption: Selecting it again does not launch a second sign-off.

shots.title: Open when ready
shots.caption: Once PM reports the window, selecting it opens the running sign-off session.

shots.title: Plan and project sessions
shots.caption: Plan, meta, guide and watcher sessions are reachable too, with the same state column.

shots.title: Scrolling a long list
shots.caption: The footer shows the position in a list longer than one screen.

shots.title: All sessions
shots.caption: Every PR with sessions, with live/known counts and attention marks, plus plan and project sessions.

journeys.title: PRs, history and timers, manual merge, busy/error/reconnect

shots.title: PRs and status
shots.caption: Open PRs with the state that matters: spec review, QA input, review loop, manual merge, blocked.

shots.title: A PR in its review loop
shots.caption: Current activity, specs, sessions and history.

shots.title: History and timers
shots.caption: PR-owned timers with what fires next ("unknown" when PM cannot tell), and recent attempts with elapsed time and outcome.

shots.title: Manual merge wait
shots.caption: Signed off with MERGE and held for manual merge. The hold has no countdown.

shots.title: An indefinite hold
shots.caption: A hold waiting for the user shows "no countdown", not a timer.

shots.title: Merge from glasses: confirm
shots.caption: Merge names the signed-off HEAD and base. PM’s gate re-checks both.

shots.title: Gate refusal (simulated head change)
shots.caption: The branch moved after sign-off. PM refuses, sign-off reruns, and the manual hold stays.

shots.title: Connection lost
shots.caption: After three failed checks (Pageborne’s rule) a banner shows how old the data is. Reading continues from the local copy.

shots.title: Actions fail visibly
shots.caption: A send while disconnected is refused and not queued, so nothing goes out later by surprise.

shots.title: Reconnected in place
shots.caption: Same document and page; nothing was resent.

shots.title: Back at the root
shots.caption: Double tap on the root page must open Even’s system exit dialog (an app-submission rule). The mockup only logs it.

shots.title: Plan review
shots.caption: Plans use the same reader. Discussion goes to the plan’s review session (plan:review:plan-sync).

shots.title: Plan approval is proposed
shots.caption: PM has no plan approval gate today, so the confirmation labels the effect as proposed.

shots.title: Changed while confirming
shots.caption: The plan changed (v5) between reading and confirming, so nothing is approved and "what changed" is offered.

shots.title: Plan diff
shots.caption: v5 added #218.

osMenu.title: OS contextual menu
osMenu.caption: Tap-then-hold opens Even’s menu with the app’s four items. On glasses the OS also adds Display off, Brightness and Close, which the simulator does not draw.
